title: Żurek
subtitle: Polish fermented rye sour soup
excerpt: A deeply sour, hearty Polish soup based on żur (fermented rye starter), served with white sausage, hard-boiled egg, and mushrooms. The signature soup of central Poland, especially associated with the Krakow region.
sourceNotes: Żurek is one of Poland's most distinctive soups, based on zakwas żytni (fermented rye sour). Closely related to barszcz biały but differentiated by stronger sourness, white sausage, and regional variations. Cross-referenced with Zuza Zak, Polska (2016).

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The soup base keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

content.text: Żurek is thicker and more assertively sour than barszcz biały, though both use żur as the souring agent. The classic garnish is biała kiełbasa (white sausage, a mild pork sausage), hard-boiled egg, and dried mushroom. In the Krakow tradition it is sometimes served in a round bread loaf with the top cut off. Bottled żur (fermented rye sour) is available in Polish food shops.

items.prepNote: or more to taste, for żur sourness
soaked in 150 ml hot water, liquid reserved

content.text: Soak the dried mushrooms in 150 ml hot water for 20 minutes. Drain, reserving the liquid, and chop the mushrooms roughly.
Bring the stock to a simmer with the bay leaves, allspice, garlic, marjoram, mushrooms, and their soaking liquid. Simmer for 15 minutes. Remove the whole spices.
Add the sliced sausage and simmer for 5 minutes.

Whisk the soured cream with the flour until smooth. Temper by whisking in a ladle of hot soup. Stir the tempered cream mixture into the soup. Add the vinegar. Heat gently without boiling until slightly thickened. Taste and adjust sourness and salt.
Place a halved hard-boiled egg in each bowl and ladle over the hot soup. Serve with horseradish and rye bread.

items.symptom: The soup is not sour enough
items.fix: Add more cider vinegar a teaspoon at a time, tasting as you go. Żurek should be quite assertively sour.

items.cause: Soup too hot when cream was added, or not tempered
items.fix: Always temper the cream by adding hot soup to it first before adding to the pot. Never boil after adding.
Make a small flour paste (1 tsp flour + 2 tsp cold water) and whisk in. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the sausage slices only to heat through (5 minutes maximum). Pre-cooked sausage just needs warming.

content.text: Żurek is strongly associated with the Lesser Poland region and particularly with Krakow, where it is served in a round bread bowl (chleb żurkowy) as a popular restaurant dish. It is also an Easter soup alongside barszcz biały, and the two dishes are sometimes confused but are distinct: żurek is more intensely sour and always includes mushrooms. The word żurek means 'little sour' in Polish, a diminutive of żur.
